name: OS username and home folder
plain: Pages cannot see your computer login name.
meaning: No web API exposes it. Proxies: file-picker display names after the user chooses a file, a downloaded file path in a native dialog, and rare leaks in error messages from extensions or file:// URLs.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: proxy: File System Access picker
fields.range: page gets file name and handle only after user choice, never a full path

fields.name: proxy: file:// URL
fields.range: pages loaded from disk can show a path in location

limits.headline: Can't see your computer login name or home folder
limits.user_action: Nothing. Pages have no way to ask for this
can: See the name of a file you pick, if it includes your name
Get your name only if you type it in
Get hints from rare leaks in extension or local file errors
cannot: See the account name from the browser
See a path from a downloaded file

story.what_it_is: Pages cannot see your computer login name or home folder.
story.for_you: A website does not know your computer user name. It might learn your name only if you type it or if you pick a file and the file name includes it.
story.for_makers: The username often contains a real name. The web gives no API for it. Sites use sign-in forms instead.

use_cases.example: A web app wanted the computer user name to greet you and asks for a profile name.
A company portal wanted the login name for single sign on and uses an identity provider.
A malicious page wanted to read the name from file paths and cannot.
A browser game wanted your OS name for a leaderboard and uses a typed nickname.
An ad vendor wanted a real name for matching and uses email hashes instead.
An exam site wanted to confirm the logged in student and uses school sign-in.
A web tool wanted the home folder path to suggest defaults and shows a file picker.

risks: Names can leak through file names

legit_uses: None: the browser deliberately withholds it
abuse: Sites attempt proxies to recover it
